title: State fusion transformer
purpose: Develop state fusion. The owner identified this family as of great importance. The method is a Set Transformer (set fusion). The goal is one fixed state from an unordered set of records, and a query against that state.
boundary: This Hero owns the state fusion transformer in code/fusion/state_fusion_transformer. The method is a Set Transformer with induced set attention and pooling by multihead attention: set fusion. The goal is state fusion. An unordered set of records becomes one fixed state, and a query reads that cached state. A caller fills SetBatch, calls encode and query, and owns the checkpoint. Hx11 owns latent-dynamics operations. Hx20 owns the Temporal Fusion Transformer in code/fusion. The State Representation Network maps one observation embedding to a predictive state and is not this family. This family has no temporal feature. A result here does not close Hx11 or Hx20.
summary: On 11 November 2026 the family is paused at a working set-to-state surface. encode writes one fixed state and query reads it. The caller owns the checkpoint, and no trained weights ship in git. make test remains the 29 October CUDA pipeline check. make capacity and make lego, run on 31 October, are separate checks: the capacity filter beat the set mean and stayed above the noise, reconstruction stayed above the visible set mean, and the Duplo miss was 0.717937 bricks against 1.04814 for the other piles, on a pile of about 1.9. A caller still chooses the records and the query answers.

goals.title: Encode an unordered set into one fixed state
goals.description: The method is a Set Transformer (set fusion). The goal is state fusion: records with explicit holes become one fixed state tensor, and a query reads that cached state. The recorded scope is the CUDA surface, the synthetic pipeline check, and the two later path checks. A caller still chooses the records.

milestones.title: Run the Set Transformer on CUDA
milestones.description: On 29 October 2026, inside the managed container, make test compiled the package with g++ against /opt/cuwacunu_embedding/libtorch 2.6.0 and CUDA toolkit 12.4 on an NVIDIA RTX A2000. state_fusion_invariance passed on cuda:0: permutation_max_abs=3.57628e-07, hole_max_abs=0, nan_hole_max_abs=0, unobserved_record_max_abs=0, padding_max_abs=4.76837e-07, two_seed_permutation_max_abs=7.15256e-07, observed_zero_gap=0.0210351. state_fusion_train then ran 400 Adam steps on one fixed synthetic panel and printed initial_masked_mse=1.25887 and final_masked_mse=1.85048e-06. That error is pipeline validation on one synthetic panel. Products are under /opt/mityane-geometrics/fusion/build/state-fusion-transformer. The image has no cmake binary. CMakeLists.txt is the build description, and the Makefile is the entry that ran.
acceptance: The package builds against the LibTorch 2.6.0 CUDA build, and the attention and training path run on CUDA.
A GPU test passes permutation invariance, shows that editing a hole leaves the state unchanged, and shows that an observed zero is distinct from a hole.
The training executable runs masked reconstruction on one fixed synthetic panel on CUDA, and the final masked error is finite and below half the initial error.
The weights are initialized here. The package does not load pretrained weights and does not depend on Nonverba.

milestones.title: Read the cached state and reload the weights
milestones.description: query answers in the same record language against the cached encode result. query_scalars is a linear probe on that answer. save_checkpoint and load_checkpoint store the config and the weights. The 29 October make test numbers stayed in force after the probe head was added. These calls do not ship a trained checkpoint.
acceptance: query reads a cached state and does not encode the set again.
A checkpoint written by save_checkpoint reloads on CUDA with a finite query_scalars gap no larger than 1e-4 on the checks that saved one.
make test remains the recorded pipeline check. The capacity and LEGO binaries are separate.

milestones.title: Record the capacity and LEGO checks
milestones.description: On 31 October 2026, in the managed container on an RTX A2000 with TensorFloat-32 off, make capacity and make lego each printed pass. Capacity filter feature 0 was 0.0925034 against a set-mean baseline of 0.348477, and above the 0.05-noise variance. Reconstruction was 0.0994731, above the visible set mean 0.0642019. The LEGO holdout was Duplo. Its miss was 0.717937 bricks against 1.04814 for the other piles, 1.94452 for zero, and 2.0558 for the catalog, on a pile of about 1.9. Both probe files stay under .temp.
acceptance: The capacity binary beats its three declared gates on the held-out synthetic panels and records that reconstruction stays above the visible set mean.
The LEGO binary beats zero, the other piles in the box, and the training catalog on the pre-declared Duplo holdout, and records that the miss is still a large share of the pile.
Neither check is part of make test, and neither ships its checkpoint.

goals.title: Decide the open questions before another run
goals.description: A later return. These questions are recorded so the next session starts from the pause. None of them authorizes a run.

milestones.title: Choose the caller's records and query answers
milestones.description: The slot names used by the checks are configuration. A later note either names the records that fill SetBatch and what each query returns, or records that the slots stay generic. This package does not settle that binding.
acceptance: The note names the records and the query answers, or states that the binding stays open.
The note leaves the Set Transformer and the encode and query contracts in place.

milestones.title: Choose whether the capacity curve continues
milestones.description: At step 1600 the filter error was still falling and remained above the observation noise. Reconstruction remained above the visible set mean. A later note either stops at that measurement or writes a new protocol before any further steps.
acceptance: The note keeps the 31 October measurement as the recorded capacity result, or states a new step count, seed, and gates before a run.
The note does not treat the synthetic filter score as a count or a forecast.

milestones.title: Choose whether a trusted count needs another width
milestones.description: The Duplo miss of about 0.7 bricks is a large share of a pile of about 1.9. A later note either keeps the one-seed state and the recorded theme, or states a different width before a new run. The holdout theme stays Duplo for this protocol.
acceptance: The note keeps the recorded Duplo comparison, or states the new width and the same holdout rule before a run.
The note does not select a new theme after looking at the score.
